newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures keep most gains, end up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures keep most gains, end up.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures weathered a sizable pullback in U.S. Treasury bond futures and the dollar's steep slide Monday, as the domestic equity market staged its second consecutive daily run to record-high prices.
June Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures bounced up to their highest point ever, at 867.20, during the morning rally as over-the-counter and blue-chip issues racked up another day of sizable gains.
The futures contract gave up some of the session's biggest gains but still managed to end up 3.35 points at 865.85, its loftiest settlement price ever.
Traders said the high-tech-inspired rise, which also drew power from technicals, caught slightly off-guard some players who had looked for a consolidative range-trade after Friday's vault upward.
"I would like to see this thing correct a little bit, but the cash stays firm," said one S&P 500s futures floor broker during the morning's busy runup.

Volume tapered off in the afternoon as futures wandered across higher ground. Brokers said stocks' seeming immunity to the drop in other U.S. asset markets made sellers leery, but the high price altitude made new buyers queasy as well.
"You're really into uncharted territory," said another floor broker.

June S&P 500 futures respected intraday support spanning the 862.50-90 area Monday afternoon on pullbacks that occasionally hit small groups of sell stops, including at 864.80, but which never gained much power.

Brokers mentioned several extrapolated levels that could thwart further rallies, including psychological resistance near 870.00, an Elliott Wave objective at 872.50, and trendline resistance drawn at 875.00, 876.00 and 877.00.
June S&Ps dipped at the opening bell, then worked upward.
The contract overnight on GLOBEX had firmed to a new record peak at 863.10 following Friday's strong bounce.

Small arbitrage buy programs emerged early as the spread over cash widened past Monday's fair value of about 1.25 points. Arbitrage buy programs needed 2.15 points over cash, and sell programs about a 0.35 point premium.
Rolling of positions out of June futures and into September, which they expected to become lead month Thursday morning, added support, brokers said.
Nikkei 225 futures slid to big losses, pressured by moderate-sized wirehouse selling in both June and September.

Brokers blamed the drop in Nikkei futures, which kept a discount to cash for much of the day, to the yen's rally tied to partly to jitters about the possibility of a rise in Japan's trade surplus with the United States.
"That was very negative for us," said a Nikkei futures floor broker. "I think it was mostly off the dollar's weakness."

June S&P 500s rose 3.35 points to 865.85, Value Lines rose 1.30 to 770.30, Nikkei fell 350.0 to 20,270.0, Midcap fell 0.30 to 283.05, NYSE Composite rose 0.75 to 451.35, Russell lost 0.75 to 390.25, and Nasdaq rose 8.45 to 957.20. ((Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
